solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carp seen by banks of Gloucester river

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outside letters of the place name are kept

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire (and another in Sussex)

explanation.surface: An angler spots a carp near the riverbanks around Gloucester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carp' looks like the fish, but it is the verb: to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain peevishly, and to grouse is the same kind of grumbling.

clue.text: Good relish that a hygienic chef had a hand in?

definitions.text: that a hygienic chef had a hand in?

parts.note: to relish something is to love it

explanation.surface: A tasty relish that a fastidious chef helped to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a hand in' sounds like 'helped make', but read literally the chef's hand is inside the item, a protective covering worn in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook wearing protective handwear for hygiene literally has a hand inside it.

clue.text: Greybeard is tired, sitting on rear of ship endlessly

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: tired as in worn out or old

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for the ship's rear is dropped

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A weary old sailor sits at the back of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A greybeard is an old man, and an oldster is an elderly person.

clue.text: I'm a star, an amazing friend to those in need

indicators.note: amazing, in the sense of bewildering, says the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A celebrity boasts about being a wonderful helper to the needy.
explanation.definitionFit: From the parable of the Good Samaritan, the word names anyone who helps people in distress.

clue.text: Ultimately criminal's bad, being recognised by cops

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word criminal

parts.note: bad means awful

explanation.surface: A criminal's awful deeds finally come to the attention of the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of criminal's is read as 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is acknowledged by the police and courts as permitted.

clue.text: A desire to get to a more advanced state

parts.note: to long for something is to desire it

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to progress further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming along means progressing, so the adverb means forward or onward towards completion.

clue.text: Embarrassed-looking drunk collared by US agent

indicators.note: to be collared is to be grabbed round the neck, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a fed is an FBI agent in American slang
a lush is a heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A red-faced drunk is arrested by an FBI man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collared' doubles as arrested in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A face gone red with embarrassment looks rosy and hot, the colour of a blush.

clue.text: Paul finally gets finale on a script for Help!

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the name

parts.note: a finale is an end
a person's hand is their handwriting, or script

explanation.surface: Paul McCartney finishes a song script for the Beatles' Help!
explanation.walkthrough: Help! is the Beatles song and film; 'gets' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch in and assist someone is to help, the imperative cry here.

clue.text: Censure maiden entering criminal hangout

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: entering says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a den is a lair or hangout
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A girl walks into a crooks' lair and gets told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like it describes the hangout, but it gives its own letters; the maiden goes into that word for a hangout.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to criticise strongly or express severe disapproval.

clue.text: Articles in The Post by foremost of sportswriters

indicators.note: by means beside, the two pieces next to each other

parts.note: a post is an upright pillar, a column

indicators.note: foremost of picks the leading letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Sports reporters lead the features in a newspaper called The Post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Post' looks like a newspaper title, but it is a pillar. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper articles written regularly by one writer are called by this name.

clue.text: Villain in car Met ordered around front of Subaru

indicators.note: around says the scrambled letters surround the next piece
ordered, as in rearranged, says these letters are reshuffled
front of picks the opening letter of the car maker's name

explanation.surface: A crook sits in a Metropolitan Police car, driven around a Subaru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns IN CAR MET into MICREANT, which goes 'around' S (front of Subaru).
explanation.definitionFit: A villain is a wrongdoer or scoundrel, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Bug messing around with printer is troubling

indicators.note: messing around with letters jumbles them into a new order

explanation.surface: A software glitch interfering with the printer is worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two words of fodder; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that disturbs or causes worry is described by both words.

clue.text: Passion is displayed in amphitheatres

indicators.note: displayed in says the letters are on show inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Passion was on show in ancient arenas.
explanation.definitionFit: In the heat of the moment means in a fit of passion: intense feeling.

clue.text: Venture must get around concerning French cap

indicators.note: getting around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to venture money is to bet it
re means concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: An instruction to an adventurer about headwear from France.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft round flat hat is traditionally associated with France.

clue.text: A drug pipe overlooked by police in Aussie backwater

indicators.note: in a down answer, what overlooks something sits above it

parts.note: the Bill (Old Bill) is British slang for the police
a bong is a water pipe for smoking cannabis

explanation.surface: Police spot someone with a cannabis pipe beside an Australian creek.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BILL is British slang for the police, from 'Old Bill'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a stagnant pool or cut-off branch of a river is known by this name.

clue.text: Do cinema up to show The Joker?

indicators.note: up, as in in disorder, says the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A cinema is being redecorated to show the Batman film Joker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to show' is a link; the definition looks like the film title or Batman's foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is a person who tells jokes, a funny man, so the definition is an example.

clue.text: I agree men must let loose animals kept for display

indicators.note: letting something loose frees it from order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that captive zoo animals should be freed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild animals kept in captivity for exhibition is a small zoo.

clue.text: After day out, flirtation becomes mutual bond

indicators.note: out says the letter for day leaves the word

parts.note: a dalliance is a casual romance or flirtation

explanation.surface: After a day away, a fling turns into a committed relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' and 'becomes' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A union formed between parties for mutual benefit is a pact or partnership.

clue.text: Island princess once seen touring northern state

indicators.note: touring means going around, so these pieces surround the next one

parts.note: Diana, the late Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A former princess tours the north of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' tells you the princess is a past one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hoosier State is one of the fifty in the USA, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Famous educational establishment rejected daughter

indicators.note: rejected, as in turned back, says the school name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is a famous English private school

explanation.surface: A prestigious school turns down a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' gives NOTE from ETON.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well known or celebrated, a famous person is notable.

clue.text: Did exercises (triceps primarily) then showered

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the muscle

parts.note: showered, as of weather, means rained

explanation.surface: Someone worked out, mainly their arm muscles, then took a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out at the gym is a way of practising or exercising for fitness.

clue.text: Revolving science room door initially is unlocked!

indicators.note: revolving means turning round, so the room's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a lab is a science room

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A revolving laboratory door turns out to be unlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlocked' means without locks of hair; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairless people have no locks, so they are humorously without locks.

clue.text: One likely to throw mud in wild garden riot

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flings mud during an unruly brawl in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw mud is to slander someone, and a slanderer belittles and defames others.

clue.text: Small boy climbing around English valleys

indicators.note: around says those letters surround the next one
in a down answer, climbing means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A little boy climbs around in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SLAD into DALS, which goes 'around' E.
explanation.definitionFit: In northern England, valleys are called this, as in the Yorkshire ones.

clue.text: Snooker player, having lost head, is a beast

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a potter is one who pots balls, a snooker player

explanation.surface: A snooker player who loses his temper is a brute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The playful river mammal is one example of a beast or animal.

clue.text: Delphi Visionary is written on bow of canal boat

indicators.note: in an across answer, written on means placed after
the bow is the front of a boat, so the leading letter is taken

parts.note: the Oracle at Delphi was the ancient Greek seer

explanation.surface: A prophecy from Delphi is painted on the front of a narrowboat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like a ribbon, but it is the boat's front.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round boat of wicker and hide used in Wales and Ireland is a type of vessel.

clue.text: Stone fireplace with flipping hot interior

indicators.note: interior says the next piece goes inside

parts.note: a grate is a fireplace

indicators.note: flipping turns the letters over, reading them backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable or hot

explanation.surface: A stone hearth gets extremely hot inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild oath in the surface, but it is the reversal signal; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard igneous rock is a common building stone.

clue.text: Chatty nurses heading to racetrack covered with turf?

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: gassy means talkative, full of empty talk

indicators.note: heading to picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Talkative nurses head off to the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' looks like hospital staff, but it is the containment verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground covered with turf is lawn-like, so it is full of green growth.

clue.text: Boris Johnson? One petitions to get rid of him!

indicators.note: getting rid of something takes it away, so a letter goes

parts.note: a pleader is one who petitions or makes a plea
him stands for Boris Johnson, then PM, cut to P for prime minister

explanation.surface: Petitioners want to oust Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter treats 'him' as the PM, giving only P; several solvers on the blog found this a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, head of government and of his party, an example of a chief.
